purpose: Provide the canonical validation report for presence and accounting of every catalog identity required by the current Character creation slice.
Verify that all 46 required identities are present, uniquely represented, bound to the expected catalog, and explicitly classified as approved, candidate, blocked, rejected, excluded, or unresolved.
Serve as the output contract for catalog-review.task.validate-required-identity-presence.
Prevent missing or misplaced identities from being hidden by aggregate catalog counts.

checks.description: All 46 required current-slice identity targets are accounted for exactly once.
Every required identity appears in its expected catalog.
No required identity key is duplicated across catalogs.
Per-catalog counts reconcile to the total of 46 required identities.
Every unreviewed candidate identity is explicitly marked candidate or blocked.
Every blocked identity references a declared active blocker.
Approved, rejected, or excluded classifications reconcile with formal identity decisions.
Presence in a catalog or fixture does not imply substantive approval.

consistencyRules.requirement: every catalog target appears exactly once
every required identity key appears exactly once in the target definition
all catalog expected counts sum to 46
executed reports contain exactly one identity result for every required target
every missing, duplicate, misplaced, or implicit candidate result references an issue
every blocked identity references a declared blocker
reportStatus counts reconcile with identity and catalog results
task completion eligibility matches the calculated report result

prototypeNotes: This artifact defines the required identity presence report and records no fabricated validation execution.
All identity targets remain unresolved until the validator scans the actual catalog artifacts.
A present candidate identity may satisfy structural presence while remaining substantively blocked.
Passing this report completes structural accounting only; it does not approve catalog identities.
Chronicle owns validation execution, issue creation, blocker reconciliation, fingerprints, stage readiness updates, diagnostics, and promotion integration.
Rule Set reviewers remain responsible for substantive source-backed identity decisions.
